value.rules_markdown:
- Each module has one responsibility, with core types in a module-local `types.rs`; every port is one trait in one file under `src/ports/`.
- Declare every CLI subcommand even when its milestone has not landed, to keep a stable surface.
- Treat presets as data, not code: add presets as new folders, never new modules.
- Never edit the `vendor/tinyagents` submodule in-tree; change it upstream and bump the pin.
- Declare examples explicitly in `Cargo.toml` with `required-features` so credential-needing tests never build in CI.
- Keep the default build offline: link no HTTP client and keep tests off the network; gate network needs behind features (`harness`, `github`, `serve`).
- Run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`, and `cargo check --locked --all-features --all-targets`.
- Use rustfmt output and Rust 2024 idioms; `snake_case` modules/files and `PascalCase` types.
- Return `Result<T>` using the crate error type from `src/error.rs`.
- Start every file with a `//!` module doc describing its role and any feature gating.
- Comments explain decisions, not code; for load-bearing flags or orderings, state and justify them.
- Public items carry doc comments; Clap fields use `///` so they become help text.
- Keep tests in-crate as `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, moving to sibling `test.rs` or `<name>_test.rs` when large; there is no `tests/` directory.
- Provide every port an always-compiled offline mock; use `MockForge` to assert on exact check runs and comments.
- Cover lane behaviour with golden tests asserting findings that survive filtering, dedupe, and capping.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behaviour.
- Keep every Markdown file at 500 lines or fewer; split and link when a topic exceeds that.
- The model never holds a write token; lanes run read-only, and write credentials are minted only in `src/apply/` after model calls return.
- Never execute contributor code; read diff and tree without building, installing dependencies, or running target scripts.
- Treat PR bodies, comments, and diffs as untrusted input; fence and label them as data in prompts; model verdicts are advisory.
- Only deterministic policy in `src/apply/` and `src/automerge/` may mutate GitHub.
- Report found secrets by type and location only; never put the value in comments, summaries, or logs.
- Use concise, imperative commit subjects and small commits; commit each coherent, validated slice on its own.
- Pull requests state what changed, any behaviour change, and how it was verified.
